Got my first swim of the year in today! My normal swimming hole had too high of a bacterial count, so I tried Fox Brook Park which I hadn’t visited before. They have bathrooms, a concession stand, picnic areas and kayak rental. Trains pass by one side of the lake roughly every hour, which I enjoyed hearing, though others might not. I don’t have enough train noises in my life anymore. Swimmers face fecal contamination at beaches along US coastline By PATRICK WHITTLE and MINGSON LAU Updated 10:15 AM EDT, August 30, 2025 OGUNQUIT, Maine (AP) — "Thousands of Americans will head to beaches for one last summer splash this Labor Day weekend, but taking a dip might be out of the question: Many of the beaches will caution against swimming because of unsafe levels of fecal contamination. "Beaches from , to , have been under advisories warning about water quality this week because of elevated levels of bacteria associated with fecal waste. The advisories typically discourage beachgoers from going in the water because the bacteria can cause gastrointestinal illness, rashes and nausea. "There have been closures this week at some of the country’s most popular beach destinations, including Keyes Memorial Beach in the village of Hyannis in Barnstable, Massachusetts; Benjamin’s Beach on in Bay Shore, New York; and a portion of the Imperial Beach shoreline near . Even on the pristine, white sand beaches of Hawaii, the Hawaii State Department of Health is warning of a high bacteria count at on the . "It’s a longstanding and widespread problem. Nearly two-thirds of beaches tested nationwide in 2024 experienced at least one day in which indicators of fecal contamination reached potentially unsafe levels, conservation group Environment America said in a report issued this summer. "The group reviewed beaches on the coasts and and found that 84% of beaches exceeded the standard at least once. The number was 79% for beaches, 54% for beaches and 71% for beaches. "The report also said more than 450 beaches were potentially unsafe for swimming on at least 25 percent of the days tested. A key reason is outdated water and that allows contamination from to reach the places where people swim, said John Rumpler, clean water director and senior attorney with . " 'These beaches are a treasure for families across New England and across the country. They are a shared resource,' said Rumpler, who is based in Boston. 'We need to make the investment to make sure that literally our own doesn’t wind up in the places where we are swimming.' "Other factors have also played a role in contaminating beaches, including increasingly that overwhelms sewage systems, and suburban sprawl that paves over natural areas and reduces the ’s ability to absorb , Rumpler said."

Il Fatto Quotidiano: “Siamo circondati dal fuoco”: il treno attraversa le fiamme, il video choc del macchinista mostra una scena impressionante Le immagini di un treno merci avvolto dal fumo e circondato dagli incendi sono diventate uno dei simboli della drammatica stagione dei roghi che sta colpendo il Canada. Il video, registrato dalla cabina di guida di una locomotiva, mostra un convoglio costretto a muoversi in un paesaggio completamente trasformato dalle fiamme, mentre il personale a bordo lancia l’allarme: “Siamo circondati dal fuoco”. L’episodio è avvenuto nell’area di Armstrong, in Ontario, una delle zone maggiormente colpite dall’emergenza incendi. La scena racconta solo una parte di una situazione molto più ampia: centinaia di roghi stanno interessando vaste aree del Paese, alimentati da temperature elevate, siccità e condizioni meteorologiche sempre più difficili. Secondo i dati del Canadian Interagency Forest Fire Centre, a metà luglio risultavano attivi oltre 800 incendi sul territorio nazionale, con una superficie complessiva bruciata superiore a 1,9 milioni di ettari. Il livello di allerta nazionale è stato portato a 4 su 5, e ha richiesto un impegno straordinario di vigili del fuoco forestali, squadre specializzate, mezzi terrestri e velivoli antincendio. Il treno attraversa il fuoco: tutti salvi gli operatori Tra le immagini più impressionanti arrivate dall’emergenza c’è proprio quella del treno merci che attraversa una zona completamente invasa dalle fiamme. Il filmato, realizzato dal macchinista, mostra il passaggio del convoglio in mezzo al fumo e al fuoco mentre la situazione appare estremamente pericolosa. La compagnia ferroviaria Canadian National ha confermato che tre treni sono stati fermati nell’area interessata e che gli equipaggi sono stati evacuati senza conseguenze. Alcuni dei convogli coinvolti trasportavano materiali infiammabili. Secondo le prime ricostruzioni, la visibilità ridotta a causa del fumo avrebbe contribuito a un incidente tra una locomotiva e il proprio convoglio, con conseguenze anche sulla propagazione delle fiamme. Le autorità stanno ancora verificando la dinamica dell’accaduto. Nonostante il rischio elevato e le condizioni estremamente difficili, tutti i membri degli equipaggi sono riusciti a mettersi in salvo. L'articolo “Siamo circondati dal fuoco”: il treno attraversa le fiamme, il video choc del macchinista mostra una scena impressionante proviene da Il Fatto Quotidiano. “We are surrounded by fire”: the train crosses through the flames, the shocking video of the engineer shows a stunning scene. The images of a freight train enveloped in smoke and surrounded by fires have become one of the symbols of the dramatic wildfire season that is striking Canada. The video, filmed from the cab of a locomotive, shows a convoy forced to move through a landscape completely transformed by flames, while crew members sound the alarm: “We are surrounded by fire.” The incident occurred in the Armstrong area, Ontario, one of the areas most affected by the wildfires. The scene only tells part of a much broader situation: hundreds of fires are affecting vast areas of the country, fueled by high temperatures, drought, and increasingly difficult weather conditions. According to data from the Canadian Interagency Forest Fire Centre, as of mid-July, there were over 800 active fires across the country, with a total burned area exceeding 1.9 million hectares. The national alert level was raised to 4 out of 5, requiring extraordinary efforts by forest firefighters, specialized teams, ground vehicles, and firefighting aircraft. The train crosses through fire: all crew members safe Among the most striking images arriving from the emergency is that of the freight train crossing a zone completely engulfed in flames. The footage, made by the engineer, shows the passage of the convoy amidst smoke and fire while the situation appears extremely dangerous. Canadian National Railway has confirmed that three trains were stopped in the affected area and that crews were evacuated without consequences. Some of the convoys involved were carrying flammable materials. According to initial reconstructions, reduced visibility due to smoke contributed to an accident between a locomotive and its own convoy, with consequences also for the spread of flames. Authorities are still investigating the dynamics of the incident. Despite the high risk and extremely difficult conditions, all members of the crews managed to get to safety.
